Commenting on her appointment, Siobhan said: “It’s a great opportunity to join Ramsdens, which has an impressive regional reputation and has achieved significant recognition over the years for providing outstanding client outcomes across the family team and wider practices.” “I’m looking forward to collaborating with colleagues who combine leading expertise with a close, personal touch, which is essential for the complex, sensitive cases the team handles.” Welcoming Siobhan, Sarah Ward head of family law said, “Having Siobhan onboard is a great addition not only to the family team, but also to the wider firm as we look to maintain regional growth momentum in Leeds and York. Her collaborative approach and impressive track record advising business owners and agricultural families further strengthen our offering in handling complex separation cases.” “It will also be a great asset as we enhance our client offering as a full-service law firm, ensuring that clients benefit from a single, trusted legal firm for both private and commercial matters.” Senior hire - (from left) Ramsdens Senior Partner, Joanne Coen; Partner, Siobhan Jeffels and Head of Family, Sarah Ward

content.title: Ward Hadaway appoints tax partner as corporate team expands
content.intro: Leeds law firm Ward Hadaway has appointed Nicola Williams as Partner advising on corporate tax and share incentives, bolstering the firm’s specialist tax expertise.
content.quote: Leeds law firm Ward Hadaway has appointed Nicola Williams as Partner advising on corporate tax and share incentives, bolstering the firm’s specialist tax expertise.
content.text:
Leeds law firm Ward Hadaway has appointed Nicola Williams as Partner advising on corporate tax and share incentives, bolstering the firm’s specialist tax expertise.
She will work closely with clients across the firms national network of offices in Birmingham, Leeds, Manchester, Newcastle and Teesside.
Recognised by The Legal 500 as a Next Generation Partner, Nicola advises on the tax aspects of mergers and acquisitions, private equity investments, reorganisations and real estate transactions, as well as employee, director and investor reward structures.
Her work focuses on reducing tax risk for buyers, protecting tax-related value for sellers and advising businesses on tax-efficient structures to retain and reward key people.
Nik Tunley, head of corporate said: “Nicola brings niche tax and share incentives expertise that sits directly
alongside the work our corporate department is undertaking. She will also bring her tax expertise to support the work of other colleagues across the firm, including in the real estate, commercial and private client teams.
“Tax advice is a key part of many transactions, particularly where businesses are buying, selling, raising investment or putting incentive structures in place. Her appointment gives us greater technical strength in this area and adds further value to our work supporting growing businesses.”
The move follows continued investment in Ward Hadaway’s corporate team, including its 2025 merger with Teesside-based The Endeavour Partnership which added scale and depth across the firm’s national network, alongside the new partner appointments of Paul Wigham and Alex Cooper so far this year.
Nicola said: “the firm is at an exciting stage in its growth. As the corporate team grows, there is a strong opportunity to extend our integrated tax offering alongside that work. I was attracted by the firm’s culture and the chance to help develop a service that works across our national client base.”
The appointment follows Ward Hadaway’s recent recognition in Experian MarketIQ’s annual M&A review, where the firm was ranked sixth nationally for completed transactions after advising on 119 deals. It was also ranked first in Yorkshire and the Northeast.
Managing Partner Steven Petrie said: “Bringing Nicola on board reflects our continued investment in specialist expertise that assists clients across the full life cycle of their business.
“As companies grow and their requirements become more complex, they need advisers who can bring different areas of law together around their corporate and commercial objectives. Nicola’s experience adds to that capability and will be a real asset to our work with businesses, investors and management teams nationally.”

content.title: The Modern Mother of the Bride
content.name: By Fashion Designer Rebecca Rhoades
content.text:
One of the conversations I find myself having time and time again is with women searching for the perfect Mother of the Bride or Mother of the Groom outfit.More often than not, they arrive feeling frustrated.

They’ve spent weeks looking at rails of dresses that all feel the same. They’ve been told what they should wear, what colours they should avoid and how they should dress at a certain age. Somewhere amongst all the advice, they’ve lost sight of the most important thing: how they want to feel.
For me, occasion dressing has never been about following rules.

The role of Mother of the Bride or Groom is one of the most important positions at a wedding. You are not simply attending as a guest. You are celebrating one of the biggest moments in your child’s life, and your outfit should reflect that significance.
I believe women deserve to feel beautiful, confident and completely themselves, regardless of age.

That doesn’t always mean wearing the loudest colour in the room or the most dramatic silhouette. Sometimes confidence comes from impeccable fit, beautiful fabric and thoughtful details. Sometimes it comes from a print that tells a story or a colour that lights up your complexion. The secret is finding something that feels authentically you.

Comfort is equally important. Weddings are long days filled with emotion, laughter, dancing and countless photographs. The last thing you should be worrying about is whether your dress feels restrictive or uncomfortable.

I also encourage women to think beyond the wedding day itself. Investing in a beautifully made piece that can be worn again for future celebrations creates a wardrobe with longevity rather than a collection of dresses worn only once.

The women I design for are not looking to fade into the background. They want elegance, sophistication and individuality in equal measure. They want to feel seen without needing to seek attention.
And perhaps that is what modern occasion dressing is really about.

Not dressing for your age. Not dressing for expectations.

Simply dressing as the best version of yourself.

content.title: The burnout blind spot smart leaders don’t see coming
content.author: By coach Ros Jones
content.name: By Coaching and personal development coach Ros Jones
content.text: They’re delivering, performing, holding it all together. The kind of leader others rely on. The one who gets things done, no matter what. And for a long time, that works. But beneath that, there’s often a very different experience that doesn’t get spoken about. Things start to feel heavier than they should. Decisions take more energy. Patience wears thinner. There’s a sense that something isn’t quite right - but nothing dramatic enough to justify stopping. This is where burnout often begins. Not with collapse, but with continuation. In my work with leaders across Yorkshire, I see this pattern frequently. The people most at risk are rarely those who are visibly struggling. They’re the capable ones, the reliable ones, the  ones who have built their reputation on staying calm under pressure and pushing through when it matters. Over time, those strengths can become part of the problem. When you’re used to handling pressure well, you don’t question it. You normalise it. You absorb it without really noticing the cost. And because you can keep going… you do. There’s often an additional layer beneath this – an unconscious, internal pressure to prove yourself, to maintain high standards, to not let people down. It can look like commitment and drive, and in many ways it is. But left unexamined, it shifts from something that supports you into something that drives you, a habitual way of being. And that’s when it can become a dangerous blind spot. Instead of noticing when things feel off, many leaders override it. They tell themselves it’s just a busy period, that things will settle down soon, that this is simply what leadership requires. Gradually, the space to pause disappears. Not because you don’t need it, but because you’ve now trained yourself not to take it. This is why smart, capable leaders miss their own burnout - because they’ve become exceptionally good at functioning inside pressure. The leaders who avoid burnout aren’t those with less pressure. They’re the ones who remain aware of how they’re carrying it, who notice when things begin to feel heavier than they should, and are willing to pause - even briefly - to reset. Because the real risk isn’t pressure itself. It’s becoming so good at carrying it… that you stop questioning whether it’s sustainable.

content.title: Bibby Financial Services appoints Gemma Heath to support SME growth
content.intro: Bibby Financial Services (BFS) has appointed Gemma Heath as business development manager, to grow its support for small and medium sized businesses across the West Midlands.
content.quote: Bibby Financial Services (BFS) has appointed Gemma Heath as business development manager, to grow its support for small and medium sized businesses across the West Midlands.
content.text:
Bibby Financial Services (BFS) has appointed Gemma Heath as business development manager, to grow its support for small and medium sized businesses across the West Midlands.
Gemma brings more than 16 years of commercial finance experience to the role, having held multiple sales positions at Lloyds Banking Group throughout her career. Most recently she served as associate director – Trading & Working Capital, Intermediaries at Lloyds Banking Group where she worked closely with brokers and introducers to meet client needs.
A specialist in Invoice Finance, Gemma holds the ABFA Foundation qualification alongside a Dunn & Bradstreet Credit Diploma and Huthwaite SPIN® selling certification. She has also built a wide network of introducer relationships during her career. Joining BFS, she has a clear focus on growing its presence in the region and continuing to fund SMEs through Invoice Finance solutions.
Commenting on the appointment, David Webb, UK head of broker and introducer, said: “BFS is in growth mode and with more than £1bn of funding capacity, we have a fantastic opportunity to support SMEs and the intermediary community in 2026 and beyond. Attracting someone of Gemma’s calibre is testament to our sales strategy and ambition.”
Speaking about her new role, Gemma said: “With the West Midlands Futures Fund seeking to supercharge projects there’s an incredible opportunity for the region’s SMEs to grow and thrive. Many of these businesses need greater access to working capital and cashflow support to enable them to seize opportunities, so I’m looking forward to leveraging existing and developing new intermediary partnerships to make this happen.
“With our strong family heritage, financing legacy stretching back almost five decades, and a reputation for supporting businesses through the economic cycle, BFS is well-placed to help SMEs overcome challenges and take advantage of opportunities
today.”

content.title: Yorkshire women in the rural landscape star at Great Yorkshire Show
content.intro: A truly inspiring Yorkshire photography exhibition which captures Yorkshire women in the rural landscape is coming to the Great Yorkshire Show, which takes place on Tuesday 14 – Friday 17 July.
content.quote: A truly inspiring Yorkshire photography exhibition which captures Yorkshire women in the rural landscape is coming to the Great Yorkshire Show, which takes place on Tuesday 14 – Friday 17 July.
content.text:
A truly inspiring Yorkshire photography exhibition which captures Yorkshire women in the rural landscape is coming to the Great Yorkshire Show, which takes place on Tuesday 14 – Friday 17 July.

Hardy and Free has been created by award-winning photographer Carolyn Mendelsohn and takes its name from a line in Emily Bronte’s Wuthering Heights: “I wish I were a girl again, half-savage and hardy, and free...” It was originally commissioned by the Brontë Parsonage Museum in Haworth as part of its contemporary arts programme and then a new series of portraits was created for Bradford 2025, UK City of Culture.

Hardy and Free will be on show in the building next to the Ariat GYS Stage from Wednesday to Friday and explores the relationship between 12 contemporary women and the natural world, all sharing a profound emotional link with the landscapes that shape them.

Over several seasons, Carolyn photographed her subjects, artists, swimmers, athletes, adventurers and activists, in their chosen natural locations. She also recorded their thoughts on why those places were important to them.
From remote moorlands to urban parks, waterfalls to working farms, these environments serve as a backdrop to narratives of resilience, creativity and identity.

Caroyln said: “I am delighted that my series Hardy and Free is being exhibited at the Great Yorkshire Show. It feels especially apt that work made in collaboration with women from Yorkshire, in landscapes that hold deep personal meaning for them, is being presented at an event so closely connected to agricultural life and experienced by thousands of visitors.

“The journey of the series reflects this  spirit first shown on an intimate scale at the Brontë Parsonage Museum, then expanded outdoors in the urban centre of Bradford as part of its City of Culture programme and now brought indoors again at large scale within the setting of the Show.

“My hope is that at the Great Yorkshire Show more people will encounter these portraits, enjoy  them and be inspired to think about their own stories, and their personal relationship to landscape.”

Tickets for the Great Yorkshire Show are on  sale now and are available to purchase in advance only, with prices frozen at the same rate as last year.

Free shuttle buses are operated by The Harrogate Bus Company every day of the Great Yorkshire Show. The buses run every 10 minutes from Harrogate Bus Station (next to the Railway Station) to the Showground’s White Gate, starting at 7.20am. The last bus departs the Showground at 7pm.

content.title: Experts earn their stripes with iconic tiger TLC
content.intro: It was once one of the animal kingdom’s most impressive apex predators and for generations has been the striped sentinel guarding the entrance to Leeds City Museum.
content.text:
It was once one of the animal kingdom’s most impressive apex predators and for generations has been the striped sentinel guarding the entrance to Leeds City Museum.

But an expert clean-up crew has discovered even the famous Leeds Tiger can fall prey to the passage of time and occasionally needs some careful pampering.

The gigantic Bengal tiger, thought to be one of the biggest taxidermy mounts of its kind anywhere in the world, was among a selection of the museum’s most precious and historic specimens being conserved in the museum’s spectacular Life on Earth Gallery.

Curators Clare Brown and Sarah Burhouse were on site carrying out meticulous checks for dust and the types of tiny pests which can be harmful to vintage taxidermy, before undertaking a delicate clean of some unique and historically significant exhibits.
A resident of Leeds for more than 160 years, the magnificent big cat was originally shot and killed in the foothills of the Himalayas by decorated soldier Major-General Sir Charles Reid in 1860.

He later boasted that it was the largest tiger he had ever seen, measuring more than 12 feet in length. Sadly, hunting tigers was a hugely popular pastime for British soldiers serving in colonial India, contributing to what was a catastrophic decline in the local population.

The animal’s pelt was subsequently shipped to the UK as a trophy and put on display in the Indian court of the London International Exhibition before being purchased by wealthy Leeds industrialist William Gott in 1862.

Gott then commissioned noted taxidermist Edwin Henry Ward to mount the tiger’s skin and presented the finished article for display by Leeds Philosophical and Literary Society, where it was hailed as “unequalled in Europe.”

As well as the tiger, conservation work included cleaning the delicate tail feathers of the museum’s incredibly rare pair of Huia, an extinct species of bird that once lived in New Zealand.

A sacred bird to the island nation’s indigenous Māori people, Huia tail feathers are traditionally only used and worn by people of great status and power.
In 1901, the Duke of York visited New Zealand and was gifted a Huia feather to wear in his hat. Unfortunately, the fashion statement led to a massive surge in demand for similar feathers, and Huai were hunted into extinction just six years later.

Also, among the animals being checked over was giant panda Grandma. Named after being captured near Weizhou village in central China, she became the first live giant panda ever to arrive in the UK in 1938. She died just two weeks later after contracting double pneumonia.

Clare Brown, Leeds Museums and Galleries’ curator of natural sciences, said: “A great deal of our taxidermy collection dates from the late 19th and early 20thcentury, and because of the techniques used to preserve the mounts, as well as what they are made
from, over time they can fall victim to pests, dust and shrinkage, where the skin dries out and can begin to crack.

“That’s why we need to carry out periodic monitoring like this to check for any noticeable changes to condition and to make sure pests aren’t causing any damage to these extremely rare and precious specimens.

“All of the animals we’ve been checking this week come from very different parts of the world and hugely varied habitats, but they’re all united by the fact their lives, and deaths were profoundly impacted by the intervention of humans into their environment.

“That’s one of the reasons taxidermy collections like ours are so important. Not only can these exhibits teach us about the past, they’re also an invaluable source of learning and research into how we can protect and preserve vulnerable species in the future.”

The Life on Earth Gallery is home to a vast collection of taxidermy which also includes a polar bear, turtle, sea lion, a Tibetan yak and the skeleton of a huge bluefin tuna.
The collection is displayed alongside information on the climate emergency and in-depth histories and stories of some of the museum’s amazing natural science objects.Councillor Salma Arif, Leeds City Council’s executive member for economy, said: “The Leeds collection is truly extraordinary and filled with a spectacular array of artefacts, specimens and stories which can be seen nowhere else in the world.

“It’s thanks to the diligence and dedication of our teams working behind the scenes that this collection is preserved and conserved so it can continue to engage and inspire visitors for generations to come.”

Leeds City Museum is a ‘Give What You Can museum’ where visitors are invited to donate to support the museum if they are able

content.name: Rachel Cheshire
content.title: Member Spotlight
content.bio:
At 34 yrs old, after spending her career in music and fashion events, Yorkshire Businesswoman member Rachel Cheshire decided to take huge change in direction. 

In February 2017, Rachel and her husband Matt’s world ended when their beautiful baby girl, Lillia, was born sleeping. “Everything came to a standstill” she said, “and during our grieving we learned that we were expecting Violet. Bringing our baby girl into the world safely was my only priority and after she was born, I was in no shape to be posing for photos or presenting on the catwalk.

“Three months into motherhood and I was bored; I was getting headaches from the lack of mental stimulation usually provided by work. I decided to start a hobby business to keep me sane because one more episode of Jeremy Kyle was going to tip me over the edge!

“A year before I had put together a cheese birthday cake for my sisters 30th birthday and people went nuts for it,” she explained. “I wanted to something that would move me into the wedding world but needed an area that wasn’t already saturated……. cheese wedding cakes it was!

“Just like Richard Branson, I wasn’t inventing anything new, I was taking an existing product but wanting to do it better! So many transferable skills were taken from years in fashion and music; profit and loss spreadsheets, photographing products, designing ideas, pitching to clients, building slide decks, planning events.

“Two years of building cheese wedding cakes flew by and then there it was…..lockdown!

“No more weddings. I had to do the thing I never wanted to do to keep our name floating about, hampers and gift boxes. Years before I had presented a show with ITV presenter and stylist, Mark Heyes. I gave him a call, and he offered to feature my products on Lorraine. The phone went crackers!
“I’ve always considered myself to be a yes person but never realised how much so until businesses began calling me about services we didn’t provide……. YES we can do that!

“Do you do cheese and wine virtual classes with a sommelier?” ……we do now.

“Lockdown saw the beginning of our grazing tables when groups of women who hadn’t seen each other in 18 months wanted to catch up with fizz and food. 

“By the time our corporate and private aviation clients came on the scene I realised we had outgrown Celebration Cheeses. All our jobs came from networking as many of our services weren’t even on our website. In November 2025 we started rebranding behind the scenes with Filament Creative to become Colourful Catering and launched February 2026.
“We’re excited to see where this year takes us, “it’s already led us to some fantastic new clients and our team is growing,” she concluded.

content.title: Former Wakefield Hospice director Awarded BEM in King’s Birthday Honours
content.text:
Helen dedicated more than 35 years of her life to Wakefield Hospice, playing a pivotal role in the charity’s growth and development before retiring in March 2025.
Her journey with the hospice began in the late 1980s as a volunteer with the Lupset Fundraising Group. She joined the fundraising team in 1990, shortly before the hospice officially opened its doors following a visit from HM Queen Elizabeth II. Over the following three and a half decades, Helen helped shape the organisation’s fundraising strategy and success, eventually becoming director of income generation and overseeing significant growth in support and income generation across the charity.
On learning of her inclusion in the King’s Birthday Honours List, Helen said: “For over 35 years Wakefield Hospice was my life. I cannot put into words what this place still means to me today and to have been recognised for my work at this wonderful charity is both humbling and overwhelming.
“Nobody goes into working for a charity to receive commendation for their work; we do it because we truly care about the cause and want to do all we can to ensure it is here to serve the local community in the very best way possible.
“That being said, I accept this honour with immense pride, gratitude and humility.
“I would like to thank all those colleagues, volunteers past and present who worked tirelessly alongside me. The kindness and generosity of the community who were always very supportive and of course my own family who have been with me every step of the way, I share this honour with everyone who has been part of my journey.
“I hope this recognition shines a light on the invaluable work of hospices and inspires others to continue supporting those who need the care.
“Whilst I remain very committed to continuing in my Deputy Lieutenant role in West Yorkshire and being a proud member of Ossett Rotary Club, to have been awarded a BEM is truly the most special way imaginable to wrap up what were some of the most meaningful years of my life.”
Helen Hirst, chair of trustees at Wakefield Hospice, said: “Helen’s contribution to Wakefield Hospice over the last 35 years has been extraordinary. Her passion, dedication and unwavering commitment have helped shape the organisation we are today, ensuring thousands of local people and their families have been able to access specialist hospice care when they needed it most.
“From overseeing the growth and development of our fundraising and retail teams over 35 years to taking on her own incredible fundraising challenges including tackling the New York Marathon, cycling through Death Valley and trekking to Everest Base Camp - this honour is thoroughly deserved and everyone connected with Wakefield Hospice is delighted to see Helen recognised in this way.”
Helen will receive her medal at an official ceremony in the coming months.
Her award recognises decades of dedication to charitable fundraising and the lasting impact of her work. The foundations she helped build continue to support Wakefield Hospice in delivering compassionate care to patients and families across Wakefield and the surrounding area.
Yorkshire Businesswoman editor Gill Laidler said. “I am delighted to hear this news and wanted to add my own comments. I have known Helen for many years and will forever remember her kindness and care when my colleague Mandy Taylor MBE who worked for Yorkshire Businesswoman passed away. Whilst Mandy was ill, even though she was not admitted to Wakefield Hospice, Helen offered kindness and support which didn’t end when Mandy sadly passed away in 2021. Helen continued to support me and other members of Yorkshire Businesswoman, ensuring that we were all OK and coping with our sad loss. I cannot think of anyone more deserving of this outstanding award.

content.title: Beyond the deal: why the best exits start years before sale
content.name: By Robin  Howcroft Financial Planner at Quilter Cheviot
pullQuotes: All right twinkle toes, what’s your exit strategy?”
content.text:
It’s a question business owners should be asking themselves too, not just those who have already made the decision to sell up, but all business owners. For leaving it late to draw up a viable exit plan can narrow down the options available which in turn can lead to a less favourable outcome being achieved. A big decision For many, selling all or part of a business is one of the biggest decisions they will ever make. Sound planning plays a fundamental role in most business successes—it’s what has got you to where you are today along with years, or even decades, of effort and dedication— but for many, the planning only goes so far. For many, it does not extend to exiting. How many? According to a 2019 study by UBS, around half of business owners surveyed did not have a formal exit strategy in place. All too often owners being underprepared for a sale can have material consequences. This can lead to selling their businesses either in a manner that does not fully compensate them for their years of effort, or the sale takes place at a later point in time than they expect. A simple solution: plan early Planning early, however, can be easier said than done. Owners tend to be so focused on the running and growing of their businesses that they can neglect longer-term personal plans. And there is no off-the-shelf plan to draw on when the time comes either. That’s because no two entrepreneurs are alike. Key considerations and plans therefore depend largely on what matters most to each individual. This can be a difficult process, and a good starting point is simply identifying what’s personally important to the owner by answering the following questions:
  • What would you like to accomplish? Who matters most to you? What legacy would you like to leave?
The answers require careful consideration and may change in time but giving them some thought can help to frame decisions in the present, as well as for the future. Popular routes for those looking to wind down after selling a business include retirement, travel and spending more time with family. Whereas those looking to carry on working may consider starting another business or becoming an employee for another company. How much is enough? Answering the above questions (or at the very least considering them), allows business owners to have a clearer idea of what they want to get out of a sale or other form of exit when the time comes. This helps inform the answer to another key question: how much is enough? Most business owners have a minimum price at which they would sell but three other factors are also key:
  • Liquidity: What are the resources required to fund your desired lifestyle? Do you have other sources of income? Will your spending increase or decrease going forward? Have you got a cash buffer for unforeseen developments? Longevity: The length of expected life after selling the business –different for a 40-year-old than a 70-year-old. Legacy – What you would like to leave behind for your loved ones? This can mean quite different things for different people.
Answers can vary depending on the aims identified in the pre-sale phase. Retirement and travel require higher sale proceeds than if going into employment for another company, for example. True, the calculations can be quite technical—essentially determining the net present value of future family spending—but the results can provide a degree of clarity which would otherwise not have been possible. And while the results may show a shortfall between the attainable sale value and the desired amount, they could also do the opposite, allowing owners to realise they are able to sell sooner than they expected. So, whether you are thinking of selling your business or you plan to keep going for a good while longer, it’s time to ask yourself: “what’s my exit strategy?” By Robin Howcroft Financial Planner at Quilter Cheviot E: Robin.Howcroft@quiltercheviot.com T: 0113 513 3973

content.title: Tackling an overgrown garden is so rewarding
content.text:
Michaela Axford our regular gardening contributor shares tips with us on what we can plant and grow ourselves.

There are few things that bring as much simple pleasure as listening to the raindrops falling on the panes of the conservatory. Following a particularly sudden and uncomfortable heatwave, the rain has been very welcome in my garden.

Following a visit to RHS last May, I was inspired to invest in a Cornus Kousa Chinensis “China Girl” - a small tree that promises beautifully creamy petals in the spring and summer. Sadly, the heatwave affected the tree quite severely despite my efforts to keep it in the shade. The leaves turned brown and wilted and the tree underwent a “false autumn” to conserve water. I really did wonder if it was the end of the road for China Girl. However, a very thorough and prolonged drenching in recent rainstorms has worked wonders. There are new leaves growing, and the tree is responding well to increased TLC. The moral of the fable is keeping the faith, and perhaps a closer eye on the weather conditions!
This growing season I have been charged with the task of restoring a small but very overgrown and neglected garden. The brief is largely my decision, but I have been asked to try to introduce elements of an edible garden. I like to consider myself a very capable and enthusiastic gardener, but I know my limits, and I enlisted the help of a professional to cut back the leggy heights of the Wiegela, Climbing Roses and hydrangeas. As Jason the gardener advised, everything was cut back but done so with the aesthetic of the cut as a priority so that the garden still retains its attractiveness. I’m the first to admit that as a predominantly allotment-based gardener, I can be somewhat brutal in my approach!

The garden is South-facing, meaning it catches a lot of sun, so I have decided to create zones. There are areas of shade treated by the placement of a shed, and upon removing a considerable number of pots and containers, it transpired that there was a rather attractive retaining wall. The perfect placement for a shade garden, consisting of white foxgloves, hostas and ferns. Knowing that the garden had been very neglected for quite some time, I did not want to take any chances with the soil. I added a great deal of fresh compost, with slow-release seaweed fertiliser dug in. Given the recent hot weather, I decided to mulch heavily around the plants to retain moisture in the soil.

As I had planned, I found a garden centre that was selling beautifully cultivated Black-eyed Susan plants. These impactful flowers are vigorous growers and tolerate full sun readily. So far, the specimen that I found has made a strong attempt to vine and this has been incredibly satisfying to watch.

In-keeping with the aim to create a partially edible garden, I also found, to my great joy, an espalier apple tree in a local garden centre. I have never cultivated an apple tree this way, so it was exciting to find one that had already been trained across a frame. The tree is planted to grow across a fence as support, and I shall enjoy training the branches along the sparse areas to fill gaps with beautiful apples later next year. The variety that I chose is “Elstar”, a partially self-pollinating variety. This is important as at present, it is the only apple tree in the garden. However, for more long-term yields of apples, it may be necessary to consider planting a dwarf variety such as a Cox’s Orange Pippin.

I was also asked to include tomatoes as part of the plan. With limited space, I have opted for container gardening. To make the most of the available space, I chose a hanging basket of Tumbling Tom and French Marigolds outside the kitchen door, with the ubiquitous favourite “Moneymaker” variety in a container in the back garden, also planted with marigolds as a companion plant. An early attempt at patio runner beans sadly failed due to a vicious snail attack in the dead of night, and it may be too late to try again at this time of year.

Possibly most exciting of all, is my tiny olive tree. Rescued from near-death for the princely sum of   £2, I have fertilised and watered this tree with all the affection of a doting parent. I have been rewarded with lush green foliage, and the early signs of flowering. All being well, and depending on the variety of the tree, we could be seeing olives growing on the tree before the summer is out. The tree - I always want to call it “she” - sits in the perfect spot; in full sun with exposure to a breeze. The wind is essential to transfer pollen from one flower to another. But who knows - with the increased in summer temperatures as our climate changes, we may just find ourselves with a bumper harvest of mediterranean fruits!

I’ll keep you updated of how I get on in the next edition.

content.title: Knights strengthen team with senior partner hire
content.intro: Knights, the UK’s leading regional legal and professional services business, has strengthened its Private Client offering in Sheffield with the appointment of Gillian Coverley as partner.
content.text:
Knights, the UK’s leading regional legal and professional services business, has strengthened its Private Client offering in Sheffield with the appointment of Gillian Coverley as partner.

Gillian joins Knights following more than twenty years at Irwin Mitchell, where she was an equity partner and held several senior leadership roles. Having built her entire career in Sheffield, she brings a strong regional network alongside extensive experience advising high net worth  individuals, professionals and business owners on wills, estate and succession planning, complex probate matters and trust administration.

Her work frequently involves advising clients with complex family circumstances as well as business owners, navigating succession and inheritance tax planning.
Gillian also works closely with charities and their supporters, advising on philanthropic giving, legacy planning and the management of charitable estates.

Gillian chose to join Knights to focus on client delivery, drawn by the firm’s model, which enables senior lawyers to spend more time advising clients and developing relationships, supported by dedicated inhouse teams.

She is a full member of the Society of Trust and Estate Practitioners (STEP) and was the only private client lawyer to be ranked Band 1 in the Chambers High Net Worth guide (2025) for Private Wealth Law in Sheffield and the surrounding area, recognising her as one of the leading advisers in the region.

Commenting on her appointment, Gillian says: “I was attracted to the Knights model as it allows for partners to dedicate their time working closely with clients and building relationships.

“Having worked in Sheffield throughout my career, I’m looking forward to building on established connections and supporting clients through increasingly complex estate and succession planning issues, as well as developing the firm’s offering for charities and their supporters.”
David Lister, Sheffield client services director, added: “Gillian is a highly respected private client adviser with a longstanding reputation in the Sheffield market.

“Her depth of experience, regional connections and strong clientfocused approach mak e her an excellent fit for Knights.”
Gillian’s appointment further strengthens the private client team in Sheffield, underlining its commitment to investing in highcalibre people who add real value for clients.

Knights is the largest legal and professional services business built for the UK regions. With 1,400 professionals working collaboratively nationwide, Knights provides multiple services to business clients alongside premium advisory services to private individuals.

content.title: Major exhibition announced for 2027 at Bolton Castle
content.text: Mary Queen of Scots: The Exhibition opens in March next year and is the first time the exhibition will be seen at a location where Mary Stuart was held. Exploring the life, legacy and enduring fascination of Mary Queen of Scots, this captivating exhibition offers visitors a journey through the dramatic life of one of history’s most iconic and controversial monarchs, tracing her story from her birth in 1542 to her execution in 1587. The exhibition combines original historical artefacts, immersive displays and striking visual design to bring her story vividly to life. The exhibition’s arrival at Bolton Castle holds historical significance. Bolton Castle has long shown rooms dressed for Mary Queen of Scots’ stay of six months – often thought to be her longest period of captivity. Her continual imprisonment and eventual beheading is seen as one of the most controversial periods of British history and Bolton Castle has always honoured her stay in Wensleydale. With displays housed within museum-grade display cases and enhanced by atmospheric graphics and period styling, the exhibition presents a compelling narrative of triumph, intrigue and tragedy. Visitors will encounter a rich collection of objects and interpretive materials that illuminate Mary’s life, reign and legacy, one that has captivated audiences for over four centuries. Jacqui Naylor, general manager adds: “This is a tremendous opportunity for the castle to host such an acclaimed exhibition and to show visitors many original artefacts which were touched by Mary, such as her rosary, a lock of hair and tapestries which are thought to have been sewn by her very hands. In addition, costumes and immersive displays bring the story alive, all now to be seen for the first time within the walls of rooms she may have known well. The exhibition also brings resonance to her sad story and a glimpse behind the royal facade at the woman herself. We are immensely proud to have this stunning exhibition from March to September and look forward to 2027.” Exhibition curator, John White said: ‘We are absolutely delighted to be staging Mary Queen of Scots: The Exhibition at Bolton Castle. The first castle to host our exhibition and a place that she knew well.’ Mary Queen of Scots: The Exhibition has been widely  praised for its ability to transport audiences into the past, combining authentic artefacts, detailed storytelling and evocative staging to create an engaging  and educational experience.  From royal intrigue and political rivalry to personal tragedy and enduring myth,  the exhibition explores the many dimensions of Mary’s life, offering fresh insights for both history enthusiasts and general visitors alike. Mary Queen of Scots: The Exhibition opens 6 March and runs to 5 September 2027. Tickets are available now for 2027 from: Mary Queen of Scots: The Exhibition | Bolton Castle

content.name: Dame Linda Pollard & Vicky Cheetham
content.intro: Leeds Heritage Theatres (LHT) is delighted to announce two new appointments, Dame Dr Linda Pollard DBE DL Hon LLD as its next chair of the board of trustees, and Vicky Cheetham as chief executive who will continue to drive the organization forward. Yorkshire Businesswoman editor Gill Laidler had the pleasure of catching up with both ladies recently and was impressed by the passion and enthusiasm both have for the future of the theatres.
content.title: The *Big* Interview
content.text:
Dame Linda will formally take up the position in May 2026, succeeding Alan Gay OBE, who concludes his final term as chair at that time.
 
Dame Linda brings exceptional experience in leadership, governance, and public service. She served twelve years as chair of Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, overseeing one of the UK’s largest and most complex NHS organisations with a turnover of £1.9 billion and 22,000 staff. In addition, she completed a Review of the NHS Counter Fraud Authority and co-authored the Messenger Review for the Department of Health. 

Dame Linda has previously held senior roles, including pro-chancellor and chair of the Governing Body at the University of Leeds and deputy chair of Yorkshire Forward. Dame Linda has also been a judge for the Yorkshire Businesswoman Awards 2024 and 2025.
 
Alongside her distinguished public service, Dame Linda has founded and led several successful businesses in marketing, property, and retail, and has been a long-standing advocate for women in leadership through An Inspirational Journey and the 2% Club UK. Her contribution has been recognised through numerous national honours, including her appointment as Dame Commander of the British Empire (DBE) in 2020, alongside awards such as Yorkshire Woman of the Year and IoD National Director of the Year (2021), the Sunday Times Non Exec Director of the Year (2024), and recently awarded Lifetime Achievement Award in the Yorkshire Post Business Awards. 
 
Dame Linda said: “I am absolutely delighted to be joining Leeds Heritage Theatres at such an exciting time in its journey. The arts are central to the identity and ambition of Leeds, and the venues play a vital role in bringing people together, nurturing creativity and celebrating our shared heritage. I look forward to working with the board, chief executive and wider team to build on this proud legacy and ensure these remarkable venues continue to inspire and engage future generations.”

Chief executive, Vicky Cheetham, said: “Dame Linda’s appointment marks an exciting new chapter for Leeds Heritage Theatres. Her exceptional leadership experience and deep roots in the region will help us strengthen our role as a creative, inclusive, and resilient organisation at the heart of Leeds’ cultural life. I look forward to working closely with her as we continue to build on our ambitions for the future.”

Beverley born Vicky is herself is new to the Heritage Theatres. Growing up in Leeds with ambitions of being a pianist or composer, Vicky studied music at Selwyn College, Cambridge University. Her first role was as an administrator at The English Concert in London, a Baroque orchestra founded by the harpsichordist Trevor Pinnock. She then moved into producing roles at The Barbican Centre delivering large scale music and dance programmes. It was then onto the Southbank Centre where over 8 years Vicky progressed through several senior leadership roles.

In 2019 Vicky joined Tate as chief operating officer and then managing director leading the organisations overall strategy and operations across marketing, digital, visitor experience, retail, management, communications, HR, finance, F&B and governance to support Tate’s artistic ambitions across all its four galleries.

After leaving the Tate, Vicky joined the Royal Shakespeare Company as interim co-executive director before joining Heritage Theatres where she is responsible for the overall strategic and artistic leadership of three iconic venues: Leeds Grand Theatre, City Varieties Music Hall and Hyde Park Picture House.

Leeds Heritage Theatres is entering a defining period of transformation, one that brings together artistic ambition, civic responsibility and the renewal of some of the city’s most treasured cultural buildings.

The strategic plan set by the ladies and the rest of the board, sets out a clear ambition to position Leeds Heritage Theatres as one of the UKs most distinctive cultural campuses, where dynamic performances, bold artistic creation and meaningful public engagement sit at the heart of the organisation. At its core is a commitment to broaden who they serve, reaching younger audiences and welcoming more diverse communities.

tips: Invest in one piece that fits properly.
Bespoke isn't just for big occasions.
content.author: Rebecca Rhoades
content.title: It’s not you, it’s the clothes...
content.text: "There’s nothing in the shops.” “I’ve ordered 20 dresses and still found nothing.” “I just want to feel nice but my body’s a weird shape.” Firstly disclaimer, every woman thinks her body is a weird shape. I can confirm, none of us are. If you’ve ever said any of the above, then maybe the problem isn’t you… it’s the clothes. There’s something about wearing something that’s been made just for you that just hits differently. Not in a loud, over-the-top way, but in a quiet confidence way. You stand differently, you feel more like yourself, and you’re not constantly adjusting or second guessing or just wishing it would fit a little better. You just feel like the best version of yourself, and I think that’s something we could all do with a little more of. Bespoke has this reputation of being out of reach, or only for big occasions, but honestly, it’s not like that. I see it as a smarter way of dressing. Instead of buying three or four things that are “okay” and never quite right, you invest in one piece that fits properly, suits your body, and gets worn again and again. I’ve worked with women of all shapes, sizes and ages especially mothers of the bride or groom who want to feel elegant, comfortable, and still like themselves. Not overdone, not ageing themselves, just right. And that’s the beauty of if everything is designed around you, not the other way round. For me, the process is just as important as the result. I design and create every piece myself, and it’s very collaborative. We talk through ideas, fabrics, shapes—what you feel good in, what you don’t, and it evolves from there. It’s not about forcing a look, it’s about finding it. This month I showcase a selection of my designs at the April Yorkshire Businesswoman event, which I’m really excited about, I do hope you were able to join us. It was a chance to see everything up close the detail, the fit, the feel of it and hopefully show that bespoke isn’t as intimidating or as inaccessible as people think. Because at the end of the day, it’s not about the dress. It’s about how it makes you feel. ✨

content.title: Heritage *Meets* Modern Elegance  at  Ambers Restaurant
content.intro: Set within the stately surroundings of the historic Cedar Court Hotel in Harrogate, Ambers Restaurant is a polished addition to Harrogate’s dining scene, one that aims to balance heritage charm with contemporary British flair.
content.text: There’s an immediate sense of occasion on arrival. First impression is heritage meets modern elegance. Following a major refurbishment investment, the restaurant has been reimagined as a stylist, softly lit space layered with earthly tones, tactile finishes and subtle nod to the building’s long history. The design manages to feel both grand and welcoming, equally suited to a celebratory dinner or an intimate evening for two. The music and a gently romantic atmosphere only heighten that sense of occasion. Ambers draws inspiration from Lady Amber Fitzwilliam, a historical figure associated with the hotel, and channels that spirit into a menu that’s both thoughtful and inventive. The kitchen leans heavily into locally sourced Yorkshire produce, presenting classic British dishes with modern technique and careful plating. Expert menus that evolve with the seasons reflecting both regional pride and contemporary tastes. The Dining Experience From the outset, the experience is elevated by a lovely warm meet and greet by host Lauren, followed by excellent, attentive service from Woody, striking that perfect balance between professionalism and genuine hospitality. For starters, I enjoyed the Ham Hock Press which was beautifully presented with a piped topping of chicken liver parfait, spiced beetroot chutney, caramelised onion, and a rich lamb jus. My guest opted for the pan seared scallops, served with charred baby leek, asparagus, and a pink grapefruit emulsion, an elegant fresh and well-balanced dish. For mains, my guest chose the Gressingham Duck Breast, served with butter glazed fondant potato, roasted squash, cavolo nero, and a spiced cherry reduction. I, meanwhile, opted for the roasted lamb rump, served with hot pot potatoes, pancetta beans, celeriac puree, caramelised onion and lamb jus. Both dishes were outstanding, full of flavour and extremely well presented. We paired our meal with a Hans Greyl Sauvignon Blanc Marlborough, an excellent recommendation from Woody that complemented the dishes beautifully. To finish, we shared a well presented cheese platter featuring five cheeses, including the mature cheddar - ‘Eh up Yorkshire’ , all served with biscuits, chutney, grapes and celery. Alongside this, we enjoyed a delightful poached rhubarb and vanilla pod crème brulee, served with a ginger stem biscuit, an elegant and satisfying end to the meal. The pacing throughout was relaxed, encouraging us to fully enjoy each course and the overall experience. This is a restaurant that understands mood by day, it offers a relaxed, almost lounge like environment for lunch or afternoon tea. By night, it transforms into a more intimate, softly lit dining room ideal for dates, celebrations, or a refined night out. In keeping with the spirit of Lady Amber Fitzwilliam, whose famous Thursday Club ran for many years at the hotel, the restaurant also hosts relaxed weekly entertainment every Thursday evening. Guests can enjoy delicious food and an elegant drinks menu alongside live acoustic music from a curated selection of artists, all within the luxurious setting of Ambers. The offering is particularly appealing, with two courses priced competitively with the option to upgrade to three courses, making it an excellent way to experience the restaurant in a more informal yet atmospheric setting. Verdict Ambers Restaurant is a confident and elegant addition to Harrogate’s food scene. It may not reinvent British cuisine, but it doesn’t need to. What it offers is something arguably more valuable: consistency, atmosphere, and a genuine celebration of Yorkshire ingredients in a beautifully considered setting. Want to try Ambers for yourself? Yorkshire Businesswoman magazine has teamed up with best-selling author, speaker and joke writer Milly Johnson who will host our ‘A Novel Lunch’ on Wednesday 6th May from 12 noon at Ambers, with guest author and Sunday Times best seller Jane Costello. Both authors will share their journey after the two-course lunch at just £55 and will sign their latest books. If guests already have books from the authors, they will be happy to sign them if you bring them along. A perfect way to spend the afternoon and with the Yorkshire Businesswoman usual networking event immediately after at 3pm where lunch guests are welcome to stay, a great networking opportunity and a chance to make new contacts. To reserve your place, visit the website https://yorkshirebusinesswoman.co.uk/join-us-for-a-novel-lunch-2026-05-06/

content.name: Vicky Clapham
content.message: Never underestimate the power of your story. It can inspire and connect.
content.role: Managing Director, Bevic Marketing and PR Services www.bevic.co.uk
content.title: Member Profile
content.bio: Long before launching my business, I was the child reading under the covers after lights out, completely absorbed in other people’s worlds. That passion led me to study English Literature and Language at Newcastle University, and ultimately into a career helping businesses find, shape and share their own stories. Today, as the founder of Bevic Marketing and PR Services, nothing compares to seeing a client gain the recognition they truly deserve. Whether it’s national media coverage, a successful campaign, or the confidence that comes from finally being seen and heard, those moments are why I love what I do. Over the past eight years, I’ve worked with an incredible range of businesses, helping them grow their visibility, credibility and impact. Along the way, I’ve hosted panel events with the BBC, secured coverage in major national and international outlets, and, most importantly, watched business owners’ step into their confidence and realise their potential. And yet, PR and marketing are still widely misunderstood. Too often, it’s dismissed as “just posting on social media” or, as Daniel Cleaver in Bridget Jones once put it, “fannying around with press releases.” In reality, it’s about far more than that. It’s about positioning, strategy, reputation and connection. Done well, it can transform not just how a business is seen, but how it grows. In a world increasingly shaped by AI, that human element matters more than ever. While technology can support efficiency, it can’t replace genuine storytelling, creative thinking or meaningful connection. Audiences don’t engage with perfection; they engage with authenticity. That belief is what led me to co-found This is Yorkshire Beauty with my friend and former client, Dr Lubna Khan-Salim. It’s a platform built on celebrating women, supporting one another, and recognising the realities of balancing business, motherhood, health and everything in between. If there’s one thing I’ve learned, it’s this: never underestimate the power of your story. It can inspire, to connect, and to create opportunities, not just for you, but for others watching from the sidelines, wondering if they can do it too.

content.name: The Editor
content.title: Cecil Beaton: Staging Icons at Harewood House
content.quote: Staging Icons offers a captivating journey through Beaton’s extraordinary career as a photographer to the stars.
pullQuotes: Beaton’s visits to Harewood in the 60s and 70s is just one example of how the site has long been a source of inspiration for artists.
content.intro:
This summer, Yorkshire’s most vibrant country house, Harewood House Trust,hosts a major exhibition dedicated to the legendary photographer Cecil Beaton (1904 – 1980). Renowned for his innovative theatrical style, Beaton captured some of the most iconic figures of the 20th Century, from Hollywood legends and stars of the West End to the British Royal Family. Organised by the National Portrait Gallery in partnership with Harewood House Trust, Cecil Beaton: Staging Icons (13 June – 4 October 2026) brings togethermore than 50 unforgettable photographs from the National Portrait Gallery’s collection, some on display to the public for the first time.

Cecil Beaton: Staging Icons (13 June – 4 October 20
content.text: Featuring era-defining portraits such as those of Audrey Hepburn, Marilyn Monroe, Fred Astaire, Queen Elizabeth II and others, the show explores how Beaton’s spectacular approach to staging and design fashioned the identities of his all-star clientele, whilst also revealing Harewood’s own connections to the photographer’s world. From the opulence of the stage to the solemn grandeur of the monarchy, Staging Icons invites visitors to consider Beaton’s approach to image-making through the art of performance and how it continues to shape identity and the public imagination today. Beaton's first love was the stage, and it left a profound mark on his groundbreaking photographic style. Using elaborate backdrops, theatrical props, costume, lighting and dramatic composition, he blurred the line between reality and artifice, transforming each of his portraits into a work of visual theatre. His passion for creating opulent sets extended to stage and costume design, bringing his unique aesthetic to numerous operas and ballets, as well as stage and film productions in the post-war period. Beaton’s bold creative vision was also instrumental in his work for the British Royal Family. Appointed royal photographer in 1939, his revolutionary portraits propelled the monarchy into the modern age, creating images that were both strikingly glamorous - demonstrated in Beaton's portraits of Princess Margaret and Queen Elizabeth, The Queen Mother as well as remarkably intimate. Just like his work in show-business, Beaton’s royal portraiture combined elegance and control with theatre, spectacle and fantasy. Staging Icons also explores Harewood’s connection to Beaton and the world of stage and screen, featuring original portraits, artworks and archival material from the Harewood collection. Throughout his career, Beaton photographed numerous members of the Lascelles family and visited Harewood on several occasions during the 60s and early 70s. Several portraits on display feature George and Patricia, 7th Earl and Countess of Harewood, who shared Beaton’s passion for the performing arts. George Harewood was a prominent figure in the world of music, and was a personal friend of many of Beaton’s sitters, such as the opera singer Maria Callas and composer Benjamin Britten. Harewood’s historic visitor book, featuring Beaton’s signature, as well as a Christmas card with a hand-drawn costume design, appears in the show, documenting the photographer's personal relationship with the family. Cecil Beaton: Staging Icons is organised by the National Portrait Gallery in partnership with Harewood House Trust, marking their first collaborative project. Featuring a number of never-before displayed portraits, Staging Icons brings the National Portrait Gallery’s internationally significant Beaton collection to audiences in the North of England. Displayed throughout Harewood’s grand State Floor interiors, this major loan is presented against the backdrop Harewood’s own renowned collection of British portraiture, including recent acquisitions such as Ashley Karrell’s powerful photographic portrait of British actor, David Harewood. This work was commissioned as part of Harewood’s Missing Portrait series that seeks to redress the lack of diversity within its historic portrait collection by commissioning new portraits of men and women of African-Caribbean heritage who have contemporary connections to Harewood. Zoë Hughes, head of public programme at Harewood House Trust, commented: “Beaton’s visits to Harewood in the 60s and 70s is just one example of how the site has long been a source of inspiration for artists. Today, Harewood continuously reimagines what makes a historic country house, and by working with the National Portrait Gallery for the first time to bring together Beaton’s work and the House’s rich history, we offer our visitors the chance to step into his glamorous world and see icons, stars, and royals amongst the beautiful backdrop of the House.” Miranda Stacey, head of national partnerships, National Portrait Gallery said “Beaton’s impact on portraiture, and how we visualise British culture, cannot be underestimated. Whether capturing a monarch or a muse, Beaton shaped the public imagination through his use of fantasy, beauty, and the art of performance. Beaton and the National Portrait Gallery share a long and distinguished history and his first major retrospective, Beaton Portraits, was presented here in 1968. It marked the first time the Gallery had ever exhibited photographs and the first time portraits of living sitters were shown, laying the foundations for our enduring commitment to photography. We are thrilled to collaborate with Harewood House Trust to bring over 50 Beaton photographs from our collection to the North, giving audiences the chance to experience the creativity, elegance, and theatricality that defined Beaton’s work.” Cecil Beaton: Staging Icons opens at Harewood House from 13 June to the 4 October 2026. For more information visit: https://harewood.org/events/cecil-beaton-staging-icons/

content.name: By The Editor
content.quote: For Bambino Mio, I would like to see it become a global leader in potty training.
content.intro: Winner of the prestigious title of Yorkshire Businesswoman of the year, the awards held at the Marriott Hotel in Leeds on 6th March is Lesley Beach the group managing director or Splash About International and Bambino Mio. Here, we learn a little more about Lesley and her career journey to date.
content.title: Meet the *Yorkshire* BusinessWoman of  the Year
pullQuotes: "In the 14 years since purchasing Splash About, the company has grown significantly with Splash About products sold in more than 40 countries"
content.text: “That route suited me very well. I was able to gain real commercial experience while studying, and by the age of 24 I was fully qualified and already working in senior finance roles. “It gave me a very practical grounding in how businesses operate day to day. I worked my way up through finance and operational roles across a mixture of SMEs and later large corporates, which gave me a broad understanding of how organisations really function. “It also made me really value that pathway as an alternative to university. At Splash About we’ve adopted a similar philosophy. Several members of our senior team joined the business straight from A-levels or university and have built their careers with us over time. “I’ve always believed that if someone is curious, hardworking and given the opportunity to learn, they can build a great career, whatever route they take.” Lesley’s first proper job was as a trainee in an accountancy practice. “I spent a lot of time visiting different businesses, helping prepare accounts and learning how companies operated. “It was a fantastic introduction to the world of business because I was exposed to so many different industries early on. You quickly learn where businesses succeed, where they struggle and how important financial discipline is.” Growing up, Lesley had no real burning ambitions for anything, but she always knew I wanted to build something in business, although she didn’t know exactly what that would look like. “I was very ambitious and wanted a role that offered a clear career path and the opportunity to progress through hard work and experience. That was one of the reasons the apprenticeship route appealed to me, it allowed me to start building that career straight away while continuing to learn. “Looking back, that drive to build something and keep progressing has probably shaped every step of my career since” she continued. “We acquired Splash About in 2011. It was still a very small cottage-industry business founded by a husband-and-wife team living in the south of France. I took out a bank loan, invested every penny I had and took around a 50% pay cut. It was a big decision and certainly a leap of faith. “In the early days I did a bit of everything, finance, operations, sales, product development and dealing with customers. I remember driving around holiday parks and leisure centres showing them our products during the first summer. We were knocked back from every single one. Most of them told me they were in a contract with a company called Swimrite Supplies Limited. I hadn’t heard of them at the time. Seven years later, we bought that company,” she laughed. In the 14 years since purchasing Splash About, the company has grown significantly with Splash About products sold in more than 40 countries and the brand has become a leader in the early years swim and learn-to-swim market. “We bought Swimrite in 2019 and made 2 more acquisitions in 2024 – Bambino Mio and our Australian Distributor, It has been quite a journey,” said Lesley. The opportunity to buy Splash About came through a former chairman I had worked with previously. He approached me about an investment opportunity and asked whether I would be interested in applying the skills I had developed working in other businesses to something I could help build myself and have an equity stake in it.” Like many businesses today, there probably isn’t a truly typical day for Lesley. “Since the acquisitions of Bambino Mio and our Australian distributor it has been something of a whirlwind, as we’ve been in turnaround and growth mode simultaneously. “My role tends to move to wherever the business needs the most support or where the biggest challenge sits at that moment,” she explained. “One day that might be a sales tender or a major retail pitch, the next it could be working through a product development issue with the design team, reviewing financial plans, or developing our longer-term growth strategy. “I really enjoy that variety. Having visibility across the whole business allows me to see how each function and project connects. “In many ways my role is simply being the business’s chief problem solver.” So, what are Lesley’s plans going forward? “I have a few clear goals for the business. “For Bambino Mio, I would like to see it become a global leader in potty training. There is a real issue emerging now, with around 25% of children reaching primary school not yet potty trained. That’s not just an environmental concern because of the number of disposable products being used, it’s also a child development issue. “We’ve developed a range of reusable potty-training pants specifically designed to support that learning journey. Our aim is to work with nurseries and parents to help children develop independence earlier.“For Splash About, the focus is continuing our international expansion and broadening the product range. We’re developing more high-tech, performance-led swim products aimed at older children and adults, building on the technical expertise we’ve developed in early years swimming.“Longer term, the aim is to build a portfolio of complementary, purpose-led brands that can leverage our global distribution footprint, while being run efficiently from our UK operations hub. “For people going into business I would say, believe in yourself and be brave. Early in your career it’s easy to underestimate what you’re capable of or wait for someone else to tell you that you’re ready for the next step. “If an opportunity comes along, back yourself and take it. And if I’m being completely honest, I would probably also tell my younger self to take a bigger loan and buy more shares. “If I were starting again, I would probably have expanded into the US earlier and invested sooner in having our own team on the ground there. “The US is an incredibly important market for both brands. Now we operate through a logistics hub, which works well operationally, but having a full office and team locally would accelerate growth and partnerships. “That is definitely something we’re looking at as part of our next phase of expansion,” she concluded. www.splashabout.com and www.bambinomio.com

content.quote: The countdown has begun as Leeds will once again become a city of stories as Leeds Lit Fest 2026 returns with nine days of unforgettable literary even...
content.name: The Editor
content.title: Leeds Lit Fest 2026 brings stories, poetry and big ideas to the city
content.intro: Running from Saturday 6 June to Sunday 14 June, the festival will bring together celebrated writers, poets, performers and audiences for a packed programme exploring everything from politics and poetry to folk horror, identity, music and contemporary culture.
pullQuotes: Leeds Lit Fest has always been about creating space for people to connect, share stories and celebrate literature
content.text:
This year’s festival promises one of its most ambitious programmes yet, with more than 50 events taking place in venues across Leeds, transforming libraries, theatres, arts spaces and community venues into hubs of creativity and conversation.

Among the headline events is an appearance from former politician and economist Vince Cable, who will reflect on politics, leadership and the rapidly changing world in what promises to be a fascinating and timely discussion. Known for his sharp insight and wit, Cable’s appearance is expected to draw audiences interested in both current affairs and the human stories behind political life.

Festival favourite John Hegley also returns to Leeds with his unmistakable blend of poetry, comedy and performance. One of the UK’s most beloved live poets, Hegley has spent decades delighting audiences with his surreal humour, inventive wordplay and deeply human observations.

Award-winning poet Kim Moore will bring her powerful and emotionally resonant work to the festival, exploring themes of womanhood, identity, resilience and the complexities of everyday life. Widely recognised as one of the most important poetic voices working today, Moore’s readings are celebrated for their honesty, intensity and connection with audiences.

Poetry lovers can also look forward to performances from the Northern Poets Collective: Nabeela Ahmed, Rachel Bower, Antony Dunn, Testament and Emily Zobel Marshall who bring a vibrant evening of spoken word and contemporary poetry; Door-to-Door Poet Rowan McCabe with his show Hard Knocks, a warm, witty and deeply personal mix of comedy and spoken word exploring community, connection and the unexpected moments that have shaped his unconventional career; and Naomi Wood with her powerful new show Monster, an exploration of the female “monster” through literature, myth and storytelling.

Alongside headline events, Leeds Lit Fest 2026 will feature workshops from World Builder David Hartley, Here Be Monsters author F R Kesby and poetry and rap star Lence; as well as community storytelling events, publishing discussions, live performances and opportunities for audiences to engage with literature in fresh and exciting ways. From intimate conversations with authors to lively evenings of performance poetry, the festival continues to champion creativity in all its forms.

“Leeds Lit Fest has always been about creating space for people to connect, share stories and celebrate literature,” said Fiona Gell, Director of Leeds Literature Festival CIC. “This year’s programme is packed with energy, variety and incredible talent. We’re especially excited to bring together such a diverse mix of established names and emerging voices, creating opportunities for audiences to experience literature in ways that are inspiring, entertaining and thought-provoking. There’s a real sense of community at the heart of the festival, and we can’t wait to welcome people back for another unforgettable year.”

Leeds Lit Fest continues to be an important part of the city’s cultural calendar, driven by a passionate volunteer team and a mission to make literature accessible, inclusive and engaging for everyone.

Tickets are selling quickly for a number of events, and audiences are encouraged to book early. Full programme information and tickets are available now at:https://www.leedslitfest.co.uk/

content.title: Vernon Kay’s ‘BBC Radio 2 Dance Sounds of the 90s Live Tour’ joins Symphonic Ibiza
content.quote: very best of 90s dance classics
content.intro: Symphonic Ibiza has today announced a major new addition to its line-up, with Vernon Kay’s BBC Radio 2 Dance Sounds of the 90s Live Tour joining the event at the Great Yorkshire Showground, Harrogate, on Saturday 15 August.
pullQuotes: Tickets are limited to an 8,000 capacity
content.text:
Already set to be one of Harrogate’s biggest summer nights, the event will now also feature a full live support show from Vernon Kay celebrating the very best of 90s dance classics in association with BBC Radio 2, giving audiences even more as part of a huge open-air evening in the Show Ring.

Best known as one of the UK’s most recognisable broadcasters, Vernon currently fronts the hugely popular weekday mid-morning show on BBC Radio 2 and of-course his Dance Sounds of the 90s show, with his live show quickly becoming one of the most talked-about nostalgia nights in the UK. Expect everything from massive singalong vocals and iconic club favourites
to big piano hooks, hands-in-the-air trance riffs and the biggest dance anthems from one of music’s greatest eras.

The addition means audiences will now experience two full-length standout shows in one evening, with Vernon Kay’s full live tour show helping launch the night before the main Symphonic Ibiza production takes over the Main Ring.

Vernon said: “I’m absolutely delighted to be bringing BBC Radio 2’s Dance Sounds of the 90s Live Tour to Harrogate this summer. The 90s gave us some of the greatest dance records ever made and there’s nothing better than getting out in front of a big crowd to celebrate them properly. It’s going to be such a brilliant night and I can’t wait to be part of it.”

Freddy White, founder of Yorkshire-based company Sound & White and lead promoter of Symphonic Ibiza, said: “We’re thrilled to be welcoming Vernon to Harrogate. To have a show of this calibre and profile joining the line-up is a huge moment for us and a fantastic boost for the event.

“It’s fantastic to be bringing the energy and recognition of a BBC Radio 2 brand into the Symphonic Ibiza arena. Vernon’s Dance Sounds of the 90s has such a strong identity and following, and it feels like a brilliant fit for what we are building at the Show Ring.

“Audiences are now getting Vernon Kay’s full live tour set as part of the evening before the main Symphonic Ibiza show begins, so it really does add another layer and make this an even bigger night out.”

Symphonic Ibiza is a landmark outdoor concert experience is coming to Harrogate this summer at the Great Yorkshire Showground for a one-night spectacular celebrating the most loved Ibiza anthems of the last three decades.

The event on Saturday 15 August will bring together the 40-piece Symphonic Ibiza Orchestra, one of the UK’s leading live dance music ensembles and a regular name at major outdoor concert events, for an evening celebrating the most iconic Ibiza anthems of the last three decades. Joined by special guests Heather Small, Rebecca Ferguson MBE and Alison Limerick,

Symphonic Ibiza will combine orchestra, live vocals and large-scale production in one of Yorkshire’s most striking outdoor settings. Tickets are limited to an 8,000 capacity to ensure an intimate large-scale experience, with the event running from 5:30pm to 10.30pm.

This will be the first outdoor music concert held at the Great Yorkshire Showground since Sir Elton John performed there in 2012. The event is a collaboration between Sound & White and The Great Yorkshire Events Centre, the Showground’s commercial events venue and grounds. Profits from events held at the Showground go to the Yorkshire Agricultural Society, the charity which organises the Great Yorkshire Show and supports farming, food and the countryside throughout the year.

Graham Thompson, commercial director at the Great Yorkshire Events Centre, said: “The Main Ring is an incredible setting and we have been working with the producers of Symphonic Ibiza on this carefully curated and locally delivered event, which is an exciting new experience for us to host.

“The addition of Vernon Kay and his BBC Radio 2 live show only adds to what was already set to be a very special evening, and we’re looking forward to welcoming audiences to the Showground in August.”

Tickets for Symphonic Ibiza are on sale now from www.symphonicharrogate.co.uk and via
the Harrogate Theatre Box Office, by phone, in person or online
at www.harrogatetheatre.co.uk.

As part of the event’s community focus, alongside supporting the Yorkshire Agricultural Society, a portion of ticket sales will also be donated to two local charitable organisations: The David Brown Foundation, a Harrogate and Yorkshire-based youth and education charity, and Harrogate Theatre Trust, supporting the continued delivery of arts and creative activity within the town.
